question: What exact-target public fd-level seek wrapper provides 64-bit stream positioning?
prototype_hypothesis: int64_t lseek(int fd, int64_t offset, int whence); AAPCS places fd in R0, leaves R1 for 8-byte alignment, places offset in R2/R3, and passes whence on the stack; result is returned in R0/R1.
callsite_evidence: IDA sub_C1C10AC @ 0x0C1C10AC is the public fs/vfs/fs_lseek.c wrapper and is called directly by many firmware callsites in the exact 3.101.036 IDB.

The wrapper resolves the current-process fd, dispatches through the fops lseek slot at +0x10, handles SEEK_SET/SEEK_CUR/SEEK_END, updates the 64-bit file position, and translates negative errors through errno storage.
IDA displays five integer arguments because the 64-bit offset is split across the AAPCS register/stack view; the recovered public prototype has three source-level arguments.
The neighboring bytes at 0x0C1C10A4 are the tail of the preceding function and a source string reference, not a separate lseek entry.
control_flow_evidence: sub_C1C10AC invokes the file-operation callback loaded from fops+0x10 and returns the complete signed 64-bit position in R0/R1.
sub_C1D8B08 passes an a5 64-bit offset and compares the complete returned pair, independently confirming the 64-bit ABI.
ownership_analysis: fd is current-process and caller-owned; offset is passed by value; no pointer ownership is transferred.
recommended_probe: Open a seekable test stream, issue SEEK_SET/CUR/END with offsets crossing 32-bit boundaries, verify returned i64 and subsequent bounded I/O position, then close.
